title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
summary: A controlled attribution benchmark fine-tuned language models on fictitious knowledge, allowing ground-truth source tracing while varying redundancy and lexical distractors. Standard document-level averaging diluted localized attribution evidence; negative-log-odds gradients with top-token aggregation improved recall in the evaluated benchmarks.
ai_technology: Language models with token-level data-attribution scoring
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: On CATT, top-token aggregation with negative-log-odds gradients improved ground-truth recall by 35–72 percentage points across several baselines; the correction also improved counterfactual retraining performance on FTRACE-TREX by up to 4.9-fold.
evidence.unknown: These results use controlled attribution benchmarks and do not establish reliable provenance for arbitrary language-model training data.
evidence.ai_role: Token-level language-model attribution scores were evaluated under controlled fictitious-knowledge, redundancy and distractor settings.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
